chapters.title: Solomon Made King
chapters.html:
1 Kings 1

Abishag

1King David was old, coming on in days. They covered him with clothes, but he could not get warm.

2So his servants said to him, "Let a young virgin be sought for my lord the king. Let her attend the king and take care of him; let her lie in your bosom, so that my lord the king may be warm."

3They searched for a beautiful young woman throughout all the territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

4The young woman was very beautiful. She took care of the king and served him, but the king did not know her.

Adonijah Exalts Himself

5Now Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, "I will be king." He got himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

6His father had never once grieved him by asking, "Why have you done this?" He too was very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.

7He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they followed Adonijah and helped him.

8But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei and David's mighty men were not with Adonijah.

9Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen and fatlings by the Serpent's Stone, which is beside En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who were the king's servants.

10But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or Solomon his brother.

Nathan and Bathsheba

11Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and David our lord does not know it?

12So now come, let me give you counsel, so that you may save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

13Go in to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, "Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'

14While you are still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words."

15So Bathsheba went in to the king in his room. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.

16Bathsheba bowed and paid homage to the king, and the king said, "What do you wish?"

17She said to him, "My lord, you swore to your servant by the LORD your God, 'Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'

18But now Adonijah has become king, and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.

19He has sacrificed oxen, fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army, but Solomon your servant he has not invited.

20As for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, to tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

21Otherwise, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted offenders."

22While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.

23They told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." He came in before the king and paid homage to the king with his face to the ground.

24Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne'?

25For today he has gone down and sacrificed oxen, fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army and Abiathar the priest. They are eating and drinking before him, and saying, 'Long live King Adonijah!'

26But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon, he has not invited.

27Has this thing been done by my lord the king, and you have not told your servant who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"

David's Oath

28Then King David answered, "Call Bathsheba to me." She came into the king's presence and stood before the king.

29The king swore and said, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life out of every distress,

30as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, 'Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,' so I will do this very day."

31Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and paid homage to the king, and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"

32King David said, "Call to me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." They came before the king.

33The king said to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord, set Solomon my son on my own mule and bring him down to Gihon.

34There let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. Then blow the shofar and say, 'Long live King Solomon!'

35Then come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne, and he shall be king in my place. I have appointed him to be leader over Israel and over Judah."

36Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so.

37As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."

Solomon Anointed at Gihon

38So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down and set Solomon on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.

39Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. They blew the shofar, and all the people said, "Long live King Solomon!"

40All the people went up after him, playing on pipes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth split with their noise.

41Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as they finished eating. When Joab heard the sound of the shofar, he said, "Why is the city in such an uproar?"

42While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came. Adonijah said, "Come in, for you are a worthy man and bring good news."

43Jonathan answered Adonijah, "No! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.

44The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they set him on the king's mule.

45Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. That is the noise you have heard.

46Solomon has even taken his seat on the royal throne.

47Moreover, the king's servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May God make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.' Then the king bowed himself on the bed.

48The king also said this: 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has given today one to sit on my throne, while my own eyes see it.'"

Adonijah at the Altar

49Then all Adonijah's guests trembled; they got up, and each went his own way.

50Adonijah was afraid of Solomon, and he got up and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

51Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon. He has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me first that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"

52Solomon said, "If he proves a worthy man, not one of his hairs shall fall to the ground; but if wickedness is found in him, he shall die."

53So King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. He came and paid homage to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."

Notes

  • v1 "old, coming on in days" — zaqen ba ba-yamim, the words used of Abraham before he sent for a wife for Isaac (Genesis 24:1).

  • vv2–4 "take care of him… the king did not know her" — sokhenet, a woman who attends and cares for someone; the word is found only in this passage (vv2, 4). Did not know her: she was not his wife, a fact that matters when Adonijah asks for her (2:17–22).

  • v5 "chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him" — what Absalom did before his revolt: a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him (2 Samuel 15:1). Adonijah was David's fourth son (2 Samuel 3:4); of those born before him, Amnon and Absalom were dead.

  • v6 "His father had never once grieved him" — lo atsavo aviv mi-yamav. The Greek of 2 Samuel 13:21, which the text follows there, says the same of Amnon: he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him.

  • v9 "by the Serpent's Stone, which is beside En-rogel" — even ha-zochelet, the crawling stone. En-rogel is the spring outside the walls where David's messengers waited (2 Samuel 17:17).

  • vv13, 17, 30 "Solomon your son shall reign after me" — David's oath to Bathsheba is not recorded before this chapter. The earlier text says only that the LORD loved him and named him Jedidiah (2 Samuel 12:24–25).

  • v21 "will be counted offenders" — chatta'im, the word for sinners, here those found in the wrong by the new king.

  • v40 "playing on pipes… so that the earth split with their noise" — mechallelim ba-chalilim, piping with pipes. The Greek has dancing in dances. Va-tibbaqa ha-arets, the earth split, the word used when the ground split under Korah (Numbers 16:31).

  • v47 "the king bowed himself on the bed" — as Israel, old and near death, bowed himself at the head of the bed after Joseph swore to bury him in Canaan (Genesis 47:31). May God make: the written text has your God, and the read form is God; the text follows the read form.

  • vv50–53 "took hold of the horns of the altar" — the altar gave refuge, but not to a murderer: you shall take him from My altar to die (Exodus 21:14). If he proves a worthy man, not one of his hairs shall fall: ben chayil, and the oath David made to the woman of Tekoa, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground (2 Samuel 14:11).

chapters.title: David's Charge and Solomon's Kingdom Established
chapters.html:
1 Kings 2

David's Charge to Solomon

1When David's time to die drew near, he charged Solomon his son, saying,

2"I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man.

3Keep the charge of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and keeping His statutes, His commandments, His judgments and His testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all that you do and wherever you turn,

4so that the LORD may establish His word that He spoke concerning me: 'If your sons take heed to their way, to walk before Me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their soul, you shall not lack a man on the throne of Israel.'

5Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether, whom he killed. He shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.

6Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.

7But show loyal love to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for so they came near to me when I fled from Absalom your brother.

8There is also with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'

9Now therefore do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man, and you will know what you ought to do to him, and you shall bring his gray head down to Sheol with blood."

10Then David lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

11The days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

12So Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was firmly established.

Adonijah's Request

13Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon. She said, "Do you come in peace?" He said, "In peace."

14Then he said, "I have something to say to you." She said, "Speak."

15He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel set their faces toward me to be king. But the kingdom has turned about and become my brother's, for it was his from the LORD.

16Now I have one request to make of you; do not turn me away." She said to him, "Speak."

17He said, "Please speak to King Solomon — he will not turn you away — that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife."

18Bathsheba said, "Very well; I will speak to the king for you."

19So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat down on his throne and had a throne set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.

20Then she said, "I have one small request to make of you; do not turn me away." The king said to her, "Make your request, my mother, for I will not turn you away."

21She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as his wife."

22King Solomon answered his mother, "Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingdom as well, for he is my older brother — for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!"

23Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, "May God do so to me and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word at the cost of his own life.

24So now, as the LORD lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house as He promised, Adonijah shall be put to death today."

25So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him down, and he died.

Abiathar and Joab

26To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you deserve to die. But I will not put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because you shared in all that my father suffered."

27So Solomon drove Abiathar out from being priest to the LORD, to fulfill the word of the LORD that He had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.

28When the news came to Joab — for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he had not turned after Absalom — Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.

29King Solomon was told, "Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD; he is there beside the altar." Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike him down."

30Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, "Thus says the king: 'Come out.'" But he said, "No, I will die here." Benaiah brought word back to the king, saying, "Thus Joab spoke, and thus he answered me."

31The king said to him, "Do as he has said. Strike him down and bury him, and take away from me and from my father's house the blood that Joab shed without cause.

32The LORD will bring his blood back on his own head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he, and killed them with the sword without my father David knowing it: Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.

33So their blood shall come back on the head of Joab and on the head of his seed forever. But for David and his seed and his house and his throne there shall be peace from the LORD forever."

34Then Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck him down and killed him, and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

35The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in his place, and the king put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar.

Shimei

36Then the king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out from there anywhere at all.

37On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for certain that you shall surely die. Your blood shall be on your own head."

38Shimei said to the king, "What you say is good. As my lord the king has said, so will your servant do." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.

39And it came to pass at the end of three years that two of Shimei's servants ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, "Your servants are in Gath."

40Shimei got up, saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to look for his servants. Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.

41Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had come back.

42The king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD, and warn you, saying, 'On the day you go out and go anywhere at all, know for certain that you shall surely die'? You said to me, 'What I have heard is good.'

43Why then have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the command that I laid on you?"

44The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your own heart all the evil that you did to David my father. So the LORD will bring your evil back on your own head.

45But King Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the LORD forever."

46Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck him down, and he died. So the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.

Notes

  • v2 "I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man" — the words of Joshua at the end of his life, Today I am going the way of all the earth (Joshua 23:14), and of the LORD to Joshua at the start of his, be strong… so that you may prosper wherever you go (Joshua 1:7), which v3 echoes.

  • v4 "you shall not lack a man on the throne of Israel" — the promise of Nathan (2 Samuel 7:12–16), here with a condition: If your sons take heed to their way.

  • vv5–6 "He shed the blood of war in peace… do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace" — shalom three times: Joab made war in time of peace, and shall not die in peace. Gray head… to Sheol, as Jacob said, you will bring my gray head down in sorrow to Sheol (Genesis 42:38). The Greek lacks He shed the blood of war in peace.

  • vv8–9 "I swore to him by the LORD… Now therefore do not hold him guiltless" — David's oath (2 Samuel 19:23) bound David; he leaves Shimei to Solomon.

  • vv17, 22 "Abishag the Shunammite as my wife… Ask for him the kingdom as well" — to take the late king's woman was to claim his place: Absalom went in to his father's concubines (2 Samuel 16:21–22), and Abner was accused over Saul's (2 Samuel 3:7). Abishag had served David in his bed (1:4).

  • v26 "you deserve to die… you shared in all that my father suffered" — ish mavet, near to ben mavet. Abiathar alone escaped when Saul killed the priests of Nob, and fled to David (1 Samuel 22:20–23). Anathoth: the priests' town in Benjamin.

  • v27 "to fulfill the word of the LORD… concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh" — I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest… I will build him a sure house (1 Samuel 2:35). Abiathar was the son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub (1 Samuel 22:9, 20), and an Ahitub was Eli's grandson (1 Samuel 14:3).

  • vv28–34 "took hold of the horns of the altar… No, I will die here" — Adonijah held the altar and was spared (1:50–53); Joab is not, as the law allows for one who has killed with intent… by cunning (Exodus 21:14).

  • v35 "put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar" — here and after v46 the Greek has long additions about Solomon's wisdom, his marriage to Pharaoh's daughter and his rule, matters the Hebrew tells in later chapters. The text stays with the Hebrew.

  • v37 "Your blood shall be on your own head" — damkha yihyeh ve-roshekha, the terms of the spies' oath to Rahab, his blood will be on his own head (Joshua 2:19). Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath (v39): David once fled to Achish son of Maoch (1 Samuel 27:2).

He said, "Please speak to King Solomon — he will not turn you away — that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife."
Bathsheba said, "Very well; I will speak to the king for you."

So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat down on his throne and had a throne set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
Then she said, "I have one small request to make of you; do not turn me away." The king said to her, "Make your request, my mother, for I will not turn you away."
She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as his wife."

King Solomon answered his mother, "Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingdom as well, for he is my older brother — for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!"
Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, "May God do so to me and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word at the cost of his own life.
So now, as the LORD lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house as He promised, Adonijah shall be put to death today."
So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him down, and he died.
Abiathar and Joab

To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you deserve to die. But I will not put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because you shared in all that my father suffered."
So Solomon drove Abiathar out from being priest to the LORD, to fulfill the word of the LORD that He had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
When the news came to Joab — for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he had not turned after Absalom — Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
King Solomon was told, "Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD; he is there beside the altar." Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike him down."

Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, "Thus says the king: 'Come out.'" But he said, "No, I will die here." Benaiah brought word back to the king, saying, "Thus Joab spoke, and thus he answered me."
The king said to him, "Do as he has said. Strike him down and bury him, and take away from me and from my father's house the blood that Joab shed without cause.

The LORD will bring his blood back on his own head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he, and killed them with the sword without my father David knowing it: Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.
So their blood shall come back on the head of Joab and on the head of his seed forever. But for David and his seed and his house and his throne there shall be peace from the LORD forever."
Then Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck him down and killed him, and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in his place, and the king put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar.
Shimei
Then the king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out from there anywhere at all.
On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for certain that you shall surely die. Your blood shall be on your own head."
Shimei said to the king, "What you say is good. As my lord the king has said, so will your servant do." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.
And it came to pass at the end of three years that two of Shimei's servants ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, "Your servants are in Gath."
Shimei got up, saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to look for his servants. Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had come back.

The king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD, and warn you, saying, 'On the day you go out and go anywhere at all, know for certain that you shall surely die'? You said to me, 'What I have heard is good.'
Why then have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the command that I laid on you?"
The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your own heart all the evil that you did to David my father. So the LORD will bring your evil back on your own head.
But King Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the LORD forever."
Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck him down, and he died. So the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.

chapters.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
chapters.html:
1 Kings 3

The Dream at Gibeon

1Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her into the City of David until he had finished building his own house and the house of the LORD and the wall around Jerusalem.

2The people, however, were sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of the LORD until those days.

3Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father; only, he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

4The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.

5At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and God said, "Ask what I shall give you."

6Solomon said, "You have shown great loyal love to Your servant David my father, because he walked before You in faithfulness, in righteousness and in uprightness of heart toward You. You have kept for him this great loyal love and have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is today.

7And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in place of David my father, but I am only a little child; I do not know how to go out or come in.

8Your servant is in the middle of Your people whom You have chosen, a great people, too many to be numbered or counted.

9So give Your servant a listening heart to judge Your people, to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of Yours?"

10It pleased the Lord that Solomon had asked this.

11God said to him, "Because you have asked this, and have not asked for yourself long life or riches, or asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to discern justice,

12I now do according to your word. I give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has been no one like you before you, and none like you shall arise after you.

13I also give you what you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that no king shall be like you all your days.

14If you walk in My ways, keeping My statutes and My commandments, as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days."

15Solomon awoke, and it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.

The Judgment of Solomon

16Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.

17One woman said, "Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth to a child while she was in the house.

18And it came to pass on the third day after I gave birth that this woman also gave birth. We were together; there was no one else with us in the house, only the two of us.

19This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.

20She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your servant was asleep, and laid him at her breast, and her dead son she laid at my breast.

21When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning, he was not my son whom I had borne."

22But the other woman said, "No, the living one is my son, and the dead one is your son." The first said, "No, the dead one is your son, and the living one is my son." So they argued before the king.

23Then the king said, "This one says, 'This is my son who is alive, and your son is dead,' and that one says, 'No, your son is dead, and my son is the living one.'"

24The king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword before the king.

25The king said, "Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one and half to the other."

26Then the woman whose son was alive said to the king, because her compassion grew hot for her son, "Please, my lord, give her the living child, and by no means put him to death!" But the other said, "He shall be neither mine nor yours; divide him."

27Then the king answered, "Give the living child to the first woman, and by no means put him to death. She is his mother."

28All Israel heard of the judgment the king had rendered, and they stood in awe of the king, because they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to do justice.

Notes

  • v1 "He took Pharaoh's daughter" — the law of the king says, He shall not multiply wives for himself, so that his heart does not turn aside (Deuteronomy 17:17). The book will return to Pharaoh's daughter among the many foreign women who turned Solomon's heart (11:1–4).

  • vv2–3 "however… only, he sacrificed… at the high places" — raq, twice: the people's sacrifice and the king's are both qualified. Bamot, high places, local altars, most often on hills.

  • v7 "I am only a little child; I do not know how to go out or come in" — lo eda tset va-vo, the phrase for leading a people: Moses asked for a man who will go out before them and come in before them (Numbers 27:17), and said at the end, I can no longer go out and come in (Deuteronomy 31:2).

  • v9 "a listening heart… to discern between good and evil" — lev shomea, a hearing heart, from shama, the word of Shema Yisra'el. To discern good and evil is what the woman of Tekoa said of David, like the messenger of God, to discern good and evil (2 Samuel 14:17).

  • vv11–13 "not asked for yourself long life or riches… I also give you… both riches and honor" — the law warns the king against piling up silver and gold (Deuteronomy 17:17); here God gives riches unasked.

  • v12 "a wise and discerning heart" — lev chakham ve-navon, what Joseph told Pharaoh to find, a man discerning and wise (Genesis 41:33), and what Pharaoh then said of Joseph, there is none discerning and wise like you (41:39).

  • v14 "then I will lengthen your days" — the promise at the end of the law of the king, so that he may prolong his days in his kingdom (Deuteronomy 17:20). This promise, unlike the gifts of vv12–13, has a condition.

  • v15 "Solomon awoke, and it was a dream" — va-yiqats… ve-hinneh chalom, the words used of Pharaoh, Pharaoh awoke, and it was a dream (Genesis 41:7).

  • v16 "two women who were prostitutes" — zonot. There was no one else with us in the house (v18): no witness, only the two women's words.

  • v26 "her compassion grew hot for her son" — nikhmeru rachamehah. Rachamim, compassion, is from rechem, womb. The same words are used of Joseph when he saw Benjamin, his compassion grew hot toward his brother (Genesis 43:30).

chapters.title: Solomon's Officials and His Wisdom
chapters.html:
1 Kings 4

Solomon's Officials

1King Solomon was king over all Israel.

2These were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;

3Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, were secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

4Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

5Azariah son of Nathan was over the officers; Zabud son of Nathan was a priest, the king's friend;

6Ahishar was over the household; and Adoniram son of Abda was over the forced labor.

The Twelve Officers

7Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household. Each one had to provide for a month in the year.

8These were their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;

9Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan;

10Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher;

11Ben-abinadab, all the height of Dor; he had Taphath the daughter of Solomon as his wife;

12Baana son of Ahilud, Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean, which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as the other side of Jokmeam;

13Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; to him belonged the villages of Jair son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead, and to him belonged the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars;

14Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;

15Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he also had taken Basemath the daughter of Solomon as his wife;

16Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;

17Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;

18Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;

19Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. There was one officer who was in the land.

Solomon's Rule

20Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea; they ate and drank and were glad.

21Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.

22Solomon's provision for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,

23ten fat oxen, twenty pasture-fed oxen and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks and fattened fowl.

24For he had dominion over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River, and he had peace on all sides around him.

25Judah and Israel lived in safety, each man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.

26Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.

27Those officers provided for King Solomon and for all who came to King Solomon's table, each in his month; they let nothing be lacking.

28They also brought barley and straw for the horses and the swift steeds to the place where it was needed, each according to his charge.

Solomon's Wisdom

29God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.

30Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.

31He was wiser than all men, than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol, and his fame was in all the nations around.

32He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five.

33He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall. He spoke also of beasts, of birds, of creeping things and of fish.

34People came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

Notes

  • vv21–34 in the Hebrew — the Hebrew numbers these verses 5:1–14; the English numbering, used here, places them at the end of chapter 4. The Greek sets much of this material elsewhere, some of it after 2:46.

  • v4 "Zadok and Abiathar were priests" — though Solomon had removed Abiathar and put Zadok in his place (2:27, 35). The list names Abiathar all the same, as the lists of David's officials name the priests of his reign (2 Samuel 8:17; 20:25).

  • v5 "Zabud son of Nathan was a priest, the king's friend" — re'eh ha-melekh, the title Hushai bore as David's friend (2 Samuel 15:37).

  • v7 "Each one had to provide for a month in the year" — twelve districts for twelve months. Judah is not named among the twelve.

  • v13 "the region of Argob… sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars" — as Moses told of Og's kingdom, sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan (Deuteronomy 3:4).

  • vv20, 29 "as many as the sand by the sea… breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore" — the sand of the promise to Abraham (Genesis 22:17), used first of the people and then of the king's understanding.

  • vv21, 24 "from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt" — the bounds of the promise to Abram, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates (Genesis 15:18). Tiphsah, on the Euphrates, is the far edge.

  • v25 "each man under his vine and under his fig tree" — words the prophets use of the age to come: They shall sit each man under his vine and under his fig tree, and none shall make them afraid (Micah 4:4).

  • v26 "forty thousand stalls of horses" — Chronicles has four thousand stalls of horses and chariots (2 Chronicles 9:25), and elsewhere fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen (2 Chronicles 1:14). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v31 "Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol and Darda" — Psalm 89 is headed of Ethan the Ezrahite and Psalm 88 of Heman the Ezrahite. Chronicles lists Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara as sons of Zerah of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:6).

chapters.title: Solomon and Hiram
chapters.html:
1 Kings 5

Solomon's Request

1Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon when he heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father, for Hiram had always been a friend of David.

2Solomon sent word to Hiram:

3"You know that David my father could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the LORD put his enemies under the soles of his feet.

4But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side; there is no adversary and no misfortune.

5So I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD said to David my father, 'Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place, shall build the house for My name.'

6So now command that cedars be cut for me from Lebanon. My servants will work with your servants, and I will pay you wages for your servants according to all that you say, for you know that there is no one among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."

The Treaty

7When Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly and said, "Blessed be the LORD today, who has given David a wise son over this great people."

8Hiram sent word to Solomon: "I have heard the message you sent me. I will do all you desire concerning cedar timber and cypress timber.

9My servants will bring it down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make it into rafts by sea to the place you direct me, and I will break them up there, and you shall take it away. You in turn shall meet my desire by giving food for my household."

10So Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar timber and cypress timber he desired,

11and Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty thousand baths of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year by year.

12The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.

The Forced Labor

13King Solomon raised forced labor from all Israel, and the forced labor numbered thirty thousand men.

14He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in relays; they would be a month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was over the forced labor.

15Solomon also had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,

16besides Solomon's chief officers who were over the work, three thousand three hundred, who had charge of the people doing the work.

17At the king's command they quarried great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.

18So Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the men of Gebal shaped them, and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

Notes

  • vv1–18 in the Hebrew — the Hebrew numbers this chapter 5:15–32; the English numbering is used here.

  • v1 "for Hiram had always been a friend of David" — ohev, one who loves, here the loyalty of an ally. Hiram had sent David cedar and craftsmen to build his house (2 Samuel 5:11).

  • v3 "because of the wars that surrounded him" — Chronicles gives David's own account of it: You have shed much blood and have waged great wars; you shall not build a house for My name (1 Chronicles 22:8).

  • v4 "there is no adversary and no misfortune" — ein satan, no adversary. Later in the reign the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite (11:14), with the same word.

  • v5 "Your son… shall build the house for My name" — the word of Nathan, He shall build a house for My name (2 Samuel 7:13).

  • v9 "I will make it into rafts" — dovrot, found only here: logs lashed together and floated down the coast.

  • v11 "twenty thousand baths of beaten oil" — the Hebrew has twenty cors of beaten oil. The Greek has twenty thousand baths, and so does Chronicles for the oil sent to Hiram's woodcutters (2 Chronicles 2:10). Beside twenty thousand cors of wheat, twenty cors of oil is a small fraction. The text follows the Greek and Chronicles.

  • vv13–14 "raised forced labor from all Israel" — mas. Later the text says of the sons of Israel Solomon made no slaves (9:22); the mas here is labor by turns, a month away and two at home. After Solomon, Israel will ask Rehoboam to lighten the heavy yoke your father put on us (12:4).

  • v16 "three thousand three hundred" — Chronicles has three thousand six hundred (2 Chronicles 2:18), and the Greek agrees with Chronicles. But each book also gives a second group of officers: five hundred and fifty (9:23) and two hundred and fifty (2 Chronicles 8:10). The totals are the same: 3,300 + 550 = 3,850 = 3,600 + 250. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v18 "the men of Gebal" — ha-givlim, from Gebal, a town on the coast north of Sidon. The Greek lacks the phrase and adds that they prepared the stones and timber three years.

speech.text: 1 Kings 5
Solomon's Request
Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon when he heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father, for Hiram had always been a friend of David.
Solomon sent word to Hiram:
"You know that David my father could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the LORD put his enemies under the soles of his feet.
But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side; there is no adversary and no misfortune.
So I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD said to David my father, 'Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place, shall build the house for My name.'

So now command that cedars be cut for me from Lebanon. My servants will work with your servants, and I will pay you wages for your servants according to all that you say, for you know that there is no one among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."
The Treaty
When Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly and said, "Blessed be the LORD today, who has given David a wise son over this great people."
Hiram sent word to Solomon: "I have heard the message you sent me. I will do all you desire concerning cedar timber and cypress timber.

My servants will bring it down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make it into rafts by sea to the place you direct me, and I will break them up there, and you shall take it away. You in turn shall meet my desire by giving food for my household."
So Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar timber and cypress timber he desired,
and Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty thousand baths of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year by year.
The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.
The Forced Labor
King Solomon raised forced labor from all Israel, and the forced labor numbered thirty thousand men.
He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in relays; they would be a month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was over the forced labor.
Solomon also had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
besides Solomon's chief officers who were over the work, three thousand three hundred, who had charge of the people doing the work.
At the king's command they quarried great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.
So Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the men of Gebal shaped them, and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

chapters.title: Solomon Builds the House of the LORD
chapters.html:
1 Kings 6

The House

1And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the sons of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of the LORD.

2The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and thirty cubits high.

3The porch in front of the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, the width of the house, and ten cubits deep in front of the house.

4He made for the house windows with recessed frames.

5Against the wall of the house he built a side structure all around, against the walls of the house around the nave and the inner sanctuary, and he made side chambers all around.

6The lowest story was five cubits wide, the middle six cubits wide and the third seven cubits wide. For on the outside he made offsets in the wall of the house all around, so that the beams would not be inserted into the walls of the house.

7When the house was built, it was built of stone finished at the quarry. No hammer or axe or any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.

8The entrance for the lowest side chambers was on the south side of the house, and one went up by winding stairs to the middle story, and from the middle to the third.

9So he built the house and finished it, and he roofed the house with beams and planks of cedar.

10He built the side structure against the whole house, each story five cubits high, and it was joined to the house with timbers of cedar.

The Word of the LORD to Solomon

11Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying,

12"Concerning this house that you are building: if you walk in My statutes and do My judgments and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will establish My word with you that I spoke to David your father.

13I will dwell among the sons of Israel, and I will not forsake My people Israel."

14So Solomon built the house and finished it.

The Inner Sanctuary

15He lined the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the rafters of the ceiling he covered them on the inside with wood, and he covered the floor of the house with boards of cypress.

16He built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with boards of cedar from the floor to the rafters. He built this within as the inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.

17The house, that is, the nave in front of it, was forty cubits long.

18The cedar within the house was carved with gourds and open flowers. All was cedar; no stone was seen.

19He prepared the inner sanctuary in the innermost part of the house, to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.

20The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and twenty cubits high, and he overlaid it with pure gold. He also overlaid the altar of cedar.

21Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with pure gold, and he drew chains of gold across the front of the inner sanctuary, and overlaid it with gold.

22He overlaid the whole house with gold, until the whole house was finished. Also the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.

The Cherubim

23In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olivewood, each ten cubits high.

24One wing of the cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub five cubits; it was ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.

25The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same measure and the same form.

26The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was the other cherub.

27He put the cherubim inside the innermost house. The wings of the cherubim were spread out, so that the wing of one touched the one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall, and their wings touched each other in the middle of the house.

28He overlaid the cherubim with gold.

29On all the walls of the house all around, in the inner room and the outer, he carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees and open flowers.

30He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, in the inner room and the outer.

The Doors and the Court

31For the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olivewood; the lintel and the doorposts were five-sided.

32On the two doors of olivewood he carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, spreading the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.

33So also he made for the entrance of the nave doorposts of olivewood, four-sided,

34and two doors of cypress wood. The two leaves of the one door turned on pivots, and the two leaves of the other door turned on pivots.

35He carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers on them, and overlaid them with gold evenly applied on the carved work.

36He built the inner court with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams.

37In the fourth year the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, in the month of Ziv.

38In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was finished in all its parts and according to all its specifications. He was seven years in building it.

Notes

  • v1 "in the four hundred and eightieth year after the sons of Israel came out of the land of Egypt" — the Greek has the four hundred and fortieth year. The text keeps the Hebrew. Ziv, brightness, is an old name for the second month, as Aviv is for the first.

  • vv2–3 "sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide… the porch… twenty cubits" — the house has three parts: the porch (ulam), the nave (heikhal), and the inner sanctuary (devir).

  • v7 "No hammer or axe or any iron tool was heard in the house" — the law forbade iron on the stones of the altar: You shall not wield any iron tool on them (Deuteronomy 27:5), for you have waved your sword over it (Exodus 20:25). Here the rule of the altar is kept for the whole house.

  • v8 "The entrance for the lowest side chambers" — the Hebrew has the middle, ha-tikhonah, though the stairs go up from there to the middle story. The Greek has the lower. The text follows the Greek.

  • vv11–13 "I will dwell among the sons of Israel" — ve-shakhanti be-tokh, the promise of the tabernacle, Let them make Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them (Exodus 25:8), here tied to a condition. The Greek lacks vv11–14.

  • vv16, 20 "the Most Holy Place… twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and twenty cubits high" — qodesh ha-qodashim, the holy of holies. The room is a cube.

  • v18 "gourds and open flowers" — peqa'im, used only for these carvings and those on the bronze sea (7:24); the wild gourds of Elisha's pot, paqqu'ot (2 Kings 4:39), are from the same root. No stone was seen: the stone house is cedar within and gold over the cedar.

  • vv23–27 "two cherubim of olivewood… their wings touched each other" — atsei shemen, wood of oil. In the tabernacle the two cherubim were of one piece with the cover of the ark (Exodus 25:18–20); these stand free on the floor, each ten cubits high, and their four wings span the whole width of the room, twenty cubits.

  • vv31, 33 "five-sided… four-sided" — chamishit and revi'it, a fifth and a fourth. Whether they describe the shape of the frames or their size in proportion to the wall is uncertain.

  • vv37–38 "the month of Bul… He was seven years in building it" — from the second month of the fourth year to the eighth month of the eleventh, seven years and six months. Bul is found only here, another old month name.

chapters.title: Solomon's Palace and the Furnishings of the House
chapters.html:
1 Kings 7

Solomon's Palace

1Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.

2He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide and thirty cubits high, on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.

3It was roofed with cedar above the side chambers that rested on the pillars, forty-five of them, fifteen in a row.

4There were window frames in three rows, and window faced window three times.

5All the doorways and doorposts had square frames, and window faced window three times.

6He made the Hall of Pillars fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a porch in front of them, and pillars and a canopy in front of them.

7He made the Hall of the Throne where he was to judge, the Hall of Judgment. It was covered with cedar from floor to floor.

8His own house where he was to live, in the other court behind the hall, was of the same work. Solomon also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had taken as his wife.

9All these were of costly stones, cut to measure, sawed with saws inside and outside, from the foundation to the coping, and from the outside to the great court.

10The foundation was of costly stones, great stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.

11Above were costly stones cut to measure, and cedar.

12The great court had three courses of dressed stone all around and a course of cedar beams, like the inner court of the house of the LORD and the porch of the house.

Hiram the Craftsman

13King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.

14He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was filled with wisdom, understanding and knowledge to do any work in bronze. He came to King Solomon and did all his work.

The Two Pillars

15He cast the two pillars of bronze. Eighteen cubits was the height of one pillar, and a line of twelve cubits measured the circumference of the second.

16He made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars. The height of the one capital was five cubits, and the height of the other capital was five cubits.

17There were networks of lattice work and wreaths of chain work for the capitals on the tops of the pillars, seven for the one capital and seven for the other capital.

18He made the pomegranates, two rows around on the one network, to cover the capital that was on the top of the pillar, and he did the same for the other capital.

19The capitals that were on the tops of the pillars in the porch were of lily work, four cubits.

20The capitals on the two pillars also had pomegranates above, close to the rounded part beside the network. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around on the second capital.

21He set up the pillars at the porch of the nave. He set up the pillar on the right and called its name Jachin, and he set up the pillar on the left and called its name Boaz.

22On the tops of the pillars was lily work. So the work of the pillars was finished.

The Sea

23He made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from brim to brim and five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.

24Under its brim, all around, were gourds encircling it, ten to a cubit, going around the sea. The gourds were in two rows, cast with it when it was cast.

25It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The sea was set on them, and all their hindquarters were toward the inside.

26Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held two thousand baths.

The Stands and the Basins

27He made the ten stands of bronze. Each stand was four cubits long, four cubits wide and three cubits high.

28This was the construction of the stands: they had panels, and the panels were between the frames.

29On the panels that were between the frames were lions, oxen and cherubim. On the frames, above and below the lions and oxen, were wreaths of hanging work.

30Each stand had four bronze wheels and axles of bronze, and its four feet had supports. The supports were cast beneath the basin, with wreaths at the side of each.

31Its mouth within the crown and above was a cubit. Its mouth was round, like the work of a pedestal, a cubit and a half. On its mouth also were carvings, and their panels were square, not round.

32The four wheels were under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were in the stand. The height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.

33The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their axles, their rims, their spokes and their hubs were all cast.

34There were four supports at the four corners of each stand; the supports were of one piece with the stand.

35On the top of the stand was a round band half a cubit high, and on the top of the stand its stays and its panels were of one piece with it.

36On the surfaces of its stays and on its panels he engraved cherubim, lions and palm trees, according to the space of each, with wreaths all around.

37In this way he made the ten stands. All of them were cast alike, of one measure and one form.

38He made ten basins of bronze; each basin held forty baths, and each basin was four cubits. There was one basin on each of the ten stands.

39He set the stands, five on the south side of the house and five on the north side of the house, and he set the sea on the south side of the house, at the southeast corner.

Hiram's Work Completed

40Hiram made the basins, the shovels and the bowls. So Hiram finished all the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of the LORD:

41the two pillars, and the two bowls of the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars;

42the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars;

43the ten stands, and the ten basins on the stands;

44the one sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea;

45and the pots, the shovels and the bowls. All these vessels that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of burnished bronze.

46In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.

47Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because there were so very many; the weight of the bronze was not found out.

The Furnishings of Gold

48Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of the LORD: the altar of gold, and the table of gold on which was the bread of the Presence;

49the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left in front of the inner sanctuary; the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of gold;

50the cups, the snuffers, the bowls, the dishes for incense and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the sockets of gold for the doors of the inner house, the Most Holy Place, and for the doors of the house, the nave.

51So all the work that King Solomon did on the house of the LORD was finished. Solomon brought in the things that David his father had dedicated, the silver, the gold and the vessels, and put them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

Notes

  • vv1–12 in the Greek — the Greek sets Solomon's own buildings after the furnishings of the house of the LORD, so that its chapter 7 runs from Hiram (v13) to the end and then vv1–12. The text keeps the Hebrew order.

  • v1 "thirteen years" — the house of the LORD took seven (6:38).

  • vv4–7, 17–20, 28–36 (the building terms) — many of the words here are found only in these descriptions (shequfim, mechezeh, shelabbim, loyot, chishurim), and the exact form of the windows, the capitals and the stands is uncertain. The text gives the plainest sense each phrase allows; from floor to floor (v7) is kept as the Hebrew has it.

  • v14 "the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali… filled with wisdom, understanding and knowledge" — the words used of Bezalel, who made the tabernacle: I have filled him with the Spirit of God — with wisdom and with understanding and with knowledge and with every kind of craft (Exodus 31:3). Chronicles calls Hiram's mother a woman of the daughters of Dan (2 Chronicles 2:14); Bezalel's helper Oholiab was of the tribe of Dan (Exodus 31:6).

  • vv15–16 "Eighteen cubits… a line of twelve cubits… five cubits" — the account of the pillars' destruction also has eighteen cubits for the pillar but three cubits for the capital (2 Kings 25:17). Chronicles has thirty-five cubits for the pillars (2 Chronicles 3:15). The Greek has fourteen cubits around. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v18 "He made the pomegranates, two rows around on the one network" — the Hebrew has He made the pillars, and two rows… and ends on the top of the pomegranates: the two words have changed places. The Greek has the pomegranates in rows on the network, as v42 lists them, two rows of pomegranates for each network. The text follows the Greek.

  • v21 "Jachin… Boaz" — Yakhin, He establishes, and Bo'az, in him is strength. Boaz is the name of David's great-grandfather (Ruth 4:21–22).

  • v23 "ten cubits from brim to brim… a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference" — the ratio of the two numbers is 3; the true ratio of a circle's circumference to its width is about 3.14. Chronicles has the same ten and thirty (2 Chronicles 4:2); the Greek has thirty-three. The written text has qaveh, the read form qav, line.

  • v26 "It held two thousand baths" — Chronicles has three thousand baths (2 Chronicles 4:5). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • vv48–49 "the altar of gold… the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left" — the tabernacle had one lampstand (Exodus 25:31); the house has ten.

Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because there were so very many; the weight of the bronze was not found out.
The Furnishings of Gold
Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of the LORD: the altar of gold, and the table of gold on which was the bread of the Presence;
the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left in front of the inner sanctuary; the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of gold;

the cups, the snuffers, the bowls, the dishes for incense and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the sockets of gold for the doors of the inner house, the Most Holy Place, and for the doors of the house, the nave.

So all the work that King Solomon did on the house of the LORD was finished. Solomon brought in the things that David his father had dedicated, the silver, the gold and the vessels, and put them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

chapters.title: The Dedication of the House
chapters.html:
1 Kings 8

The Ark Brought into the House

1Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' houses of the sons of Israel, before King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the City of David, which is Zion.

2All the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon at the feast in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.

3All the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.

4They brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.

5King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered before him were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, so many that they could not be counted or numbered.

6Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, the Most Holy Place, under the wings of the cherubim.

7For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.

8The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place in front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from outside. They are there to this day.

9There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.

10And it came to pass, when the priests came out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD,

11so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

12Then Solomon said,
"The LORD has said that He would dwell in thick darkness.

13I have surely built You an exalted house,
a place for You to dwell in forever."

Solomon Blesses the Assembly

14Then the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.

15He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to David my father, and with His hand has fulfilled it, saying,

16'Since the day that I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, so that My name might be there. But I have chosen Jerusalem, that My name might be there, and I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.'

17It was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

18But the LORD said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, you did well that it was in your heart.

19Only, you shall not build the house, but your son who shall come from your body, he shall build the house for My name.'

20Now the LORD has fulfilled His word that He spoke: I have risen in place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

21There I have made a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt."

Solomon's Prayer

22Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward the heavens,

23and said, "O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in the heavens above or on the earth beneath, keeping covenant and loyal love with Your servants who walk before You with all their heart,

24who have kept with Your servant David my father what You promised him. You spoke with Your mouth, and with Your hand You have fulfilled it this day.

25And now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep with Your servant David my father what You promised him, saying, 'You shall not lack a man before Me to sit on the throne of Israel, if only your sons take heed to their way, to walk before Me as you have walked before Me.'

26And now, O God of Israel, let Your word be confirmed, which You spoke to Your servant David my father.

27But will God indeed dwell on the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You; how much less this house that I have built!

28Yet turn toward the prayer of Your servant and his plea, O LORD my God, to listen to the cry and the prayer that Your servant prays before You today,

29that Your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, toward the place of which You have said, 'My name shall be there,' to listen to the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.

30Listen to the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear in the place of Your dwelling, in the heavens; hear and forgive.

31If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath, and comes and swears his oath before Your altar in this house,

32then hear in the heavens and act, and judge Your servants, condemning the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.

33When Your people Israel are struck down before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they turn back to You and confess Your name and pray and plead with You in this house,

34then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that You gave to their fathers.

35When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name and turn from their sin because You afflict them,

36then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, when You teach them the good way in which they should walk, and give rain on Your land that You have given to Your people as an inheritance.

37If there is famine in the land, if there is plague, scorching or mildew, locust or grasshopper, if their enemy besieges them in the land of their gates, whatever blow, whatever sickness there is,

38whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any man of all Your people Israel, each knowing the blow of his own heart and spreading out his hands toward this house,

39then hear in the heavens, the place of Your dwelling, and forgive and act, and give to each man according to all his ways, whose heart You know — for You, You alone, know the hearts of all the sons of men —

40so that they may fear You all the days that they live on the face of the land that You gave to our fathers.

41Also concerning the foreigner, who is not of Your people Israel, but comes from a far country for Your name's sake —

42for they shall hear of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your outstretched arm — when he comes and prays toward this house,

43hear in the heavens, the place of Your dwelling, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to You for, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and may know that this house that I have built is called by Your name.

44When Your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way You send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city that You have chosen and the house that I have built for Your name,

45then hear in the heavens their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.

46When they sin against You — for there is no man who does not sin — and You are angry with them and give them to an enemy, so that their captors carry them away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near,

47yet if they take it to heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and turn back and plead with You in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and have done wrong; we have acted wickedly,'

48and if they turn back to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies who carried them captive, and pray to You toward their land, which You gave to their fathers, the city that You have chosen and the house that I have built for Your name,

49then hear in the heavens, the place of Your dwelling, their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause,

50and forgive Your people who have sinned against You, and all their transgressions that they have committed against You, and grant them compassion before their captors, so that they may have compassion on them.

51For they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out of Egypt, from the middle of the iron furnace.

52Let Your eyes be open to the plea of Your servant and to the plea of Your people Israel, to listen to them whenever they call to You.

53For You set them apart from all the peoples of the earth to be Your inheritance, as You spoke through Moses Your servant when You brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord GOD."

The Blessing and the Sacrifices

54And it came to pass, when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and plea to the LORD, that he rose from before the altar of the LORD, where he had knelt with his hands spread out toward the heavens.

55He stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,

56"Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel, according to all that He promised. Not one word has failed of all His good word that He spoke through Moses His servant.

57May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He not leave us or forsake us,

58so that He may incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways and to keep His commandments, His statutes and His judgments, which He commanded our fathers.

59Let these words of mine, with which I have pleaded before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires,

60so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God; there is no other.

61Let your heart therefore be whole with the LORD our God, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments, as at this day."

62Then the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the LORD.

63Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.

64The same day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before the LORD was too small to hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings.

65So Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt, before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.

66On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king and went to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the good that the LORD had done for David His servant and for Israel His people.

Notes

  • v2 "in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month" — Etanim, found only here, another of the old month names (Ziv and Bul, 6:1, 38). The feast of the seventh month is the Festival of Booths (Leviticus 23:34). The house was finished in the eighth month (6:38), so this is a later year; the Greek opens the chapter when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and his own house, after twenty years (7:1; 6:38).

  • vv10–11 "the cloud filled the house of the LORD… the priests could not stand to minister" — as when the tabernacle was set up: Moses could not come into the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of the LORD filled the dwelling (Exodus 40:35).

  • vv12–13 "He would dwell in thick darkness… an exalted house" — ba-arafel, the darkness Moses entered on Sinai, Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was (Exodus 20:21). Beit zevul, a house of loftiness. The Greek places these lines after v53, begins them The LORD set the sun in the heavens, and ends them Is it not written in the book of the song?

  • v16 "But I have chosen Jerusalem, that My name might be there, and" — the Hebrew lacks these words, going from so that My name might be there straight to and I have chosen David. The Greek has them, and so does Chronicles (2 Chronicles 6:5–6). The two clauses end alike, le-hiyot shemi sham, and the eye can pass from the first to the second. The text follows the Greek and Chronicles.

  • v27 "The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You" — shemei ha-shamayim, the heavens of the heavens. The prayer that dedicates the house says first that no house can hold God; what it asks is that He hear in the heavens (vv30, 32, 34 and on).

  • v37 "scorching or mildew" — shiddafon yeraqon, the pair of blights in the covenant curses, with scorching and with mildew (Deuteronomy 28:22).

  • vv46–47 "for there is no man who does not sin… We have sinned and have done wrong; we have acted wickedly" — chatanu ve-he'evinu rasha'nu, three verbs of confession. The prayer foresees exile to the land of the enemy, and repentance there.

  • v51 "from the middle of the iron furnace" — mi-tokh kur ha-barzel, the figure of Egypt in brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be a people of His own inheritance (Deuteronomy 4:20).

  • v56 "Not one word has failed of all His good word" — as at the end of the conquest, Not one word failed of all the good word that the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel (Joshua 21:45).

  • vv65–66 "seven days and seven days, fourteen days… On the eighth day" — Chronicles explains: the dedication of the altar they kept seven days, and the feast seven days, and the people were sent home on the twenty-third day of the seventh month (2 Chronicles 7:9–10). The Greek has only seven days. The text keeps the Hebrew.
